extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting papers to ACL conferences (review and final/camera-ready versions)
extracted.subtask_description: Formatting and submission requirements for review and final versions of papers to ACL conferences, covering page limits, PDF requirements, layout, fonts, metadata, sections like Limitations, appendices, supplementary material, and citation/reference conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use provided style files
rubrics_metrics.description: ACL provides style files for LaTeX and Microsoft Word that meet these requirements. We strongly recommend the use of these style files, which have been appropriately tailored for the *ACL proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style files are available at https://github.com/acl-org/acl-style-files. Use them to ensure compliance with formatting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper length — long papers (review and final)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review versions of long papers may have up to eight (8) pages of content plus unlimited pages for references. Upon acceptance, final versions of long papers will be given one additional page – up to nine (9) pages of content plus unlimited pages for acknowledgments and references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All figures and tables that are part of the main text must fit within these page limits. Papers that do not conform to these requirements may be rejected without review. Workshop chairs may set different rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper length — short papers (review and final)
rubrics_metrics.description: Review versions of short papers may have up to four (4) pages of content, plus unlimited pages for references. Final versions of short papers may have up to five (5) pages, plus unlimited pages for acknowledgments and references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All figures and tables that are part of the main text must fit within these page limits. Appendices and supplementary material encouraged but review versions must be self-contained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-contained review version
rubrics_metrics.description: Review versions of papers must be self-contained: it is optional for reviewers to look at appendices or supplementary material. Review versions should not refer, for further detail, to documents, code or data resources that are not available to the reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary material is available but reviewers are not required to consult it; do not place essential content outside the main review PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: File format — PDF with embedded fonts
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers must be in Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF). Please make sure that your PDF file embeds all necessary fonts, especially for tree diagrams, symbols, and Asian languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using Asian fonts, they must be embedded. START will not let you upload your final PDF without all fonts embedded. Check with pdffonts mypaper.pdf and confirm 'yes' under 'emb' for all fonts. Test by viewing/printing on another machine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper size — A4 required
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers must use A4 paper format (21 cm x 29.7 cm). Papers must not be submitted with any other paper size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check using pdfinfo (Page size: 595.276 x 841.89 pts), Apple Preview inspector (8.27 x 11.7 inches), or Adobe Acrobat File → Properties (8.27 × 11.69 in). Contact publication chairs if you cannot meet this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layout — margins, columns and dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: All text except for page numbers must fit within the margins. Manuscripts must be set in two columns. Exceptions: title, authors’ names and complete addresses (centered at top of first page), and any full-width figures or tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exact dimensions on A4: Left/Right/Top/Bottom margins = 2.5 cm; Column width = 7.7 cm; Column height = 24.7 cm; Gap between columns = 0.6 cm. Wide figures/tables may run across both columns and must be at least one column wide (no wrapped text within a column).

rubrics_metrics.name: Page numbers and ruler for review/final
rubrics_metrics.description: Review versions should have page numbers, centered in the bottom margin, and a ruler (line numbers in the left and right margins) so reviewers may comment on particular lines. The final version should not contain page numbers or a ruler.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ruler should not change appearance of other content. If ruler measurements do not align well, fractional references (e.g., 'line 295.5') may be used by reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ruler/anonymity handling in appendices/supplementary
rubrics_metrics.description: Review versions of appendices and supplementary material must follow the same anonymity guidelines as the main paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include author-identifying information in review appendices or supplementary uploads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fonts — Times Roman preferred
rubrics_metrics.description: All text (except non-Latin scripts and mathematical formulas) should be set in Times Roman. If Times Roman is unavailable, use Times New Roman or Computer Modern Roman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For any text or numbers in tables and figures, whenever possible use the document text font size; text should be clearly readable when printed on A4. Submissions that abuse font size/spacing or use non-human-visible text may be desk rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font sizes and styles for document elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified font sizes and styles must be used for each type of text in the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table of required sizes/styles: paper title 15 pt bold; author names 12 pt bold; author affiliation 12 pt; the word 'Abstract' 12 pt bold; section titles 12 pt bold; subsection titles 11 pt bold; document text 11 pt; captions 10 pt; abstract text 10 pt; bibliography 10 pt; footnotes 9 pt. Ensure figure/table text/readability aligns with these rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and authors formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the ACL style file: center the title and the author name(s) and affiliation(s) across both columns. Place the title centered at the top of the first page, in 15-point bold, 2.5 cm from the top.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long titles may be typed on two lines without blank lines. Write the title in title case; do not write the title in all capitals except for normal acronyms. Title should contain only plain text without extra markup or LaTeX commands. Place author names and affiliation under the title; write full given names (no initials unless normally used), do not format surnames in all capitals, do not use footnotes for affiliations. Affiliation should contain the author's complete address and, if possible, an email. Title/authors should be identical to submission website entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract formatting and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Type the abstract at the beginning of the first column. Center the word 'Abstract' in 12 point bold above the abstract body. The width of the abstract should be smaller than the normal column width by 0.6 cm on each side. The abstract text should be 10 point roman, single-spaced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract should be a concise summary of the general thesis and conclusions of the paper and should be no longer than 200 words. Abstracts should contain only plain text without extra markup and LaTeX commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metadata plain Unicode requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The title and abstract in the main text can include (La)TeX commands, but the same content needs to be entered into platforms (ARR camera-ready form, OpenReview, ACL Anthology) as plain Unicode text only, without HTML tags or (La)TeX commands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If plain Unicode cannot match PDF verbatim, approximate closely. Tools like unicodeit.net can help. Examples of disallowed and allowed forms are provided (e.g., use S³ not S$^3$; avoid <sup> tags).

rubrics_metrics.name: Main text formatting (paragraphs and spacing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin the main body immediately after the abstract, in two columns. The text should be 11 point roman, single-spaced. Indent 0.4 cm when starting a new paragraph, except for the first paragraph in a section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use numbered sections with Arabic numerals for easy cross-referencing (e.g., '1 Introduction', '6.1 File Format').

rubrics_metrics.name: Sections and subsection numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Use numbered sections (Arabic numerals) and number subsections with the section number and subsection number separated by a dot, in Arabic numerals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps cross-references and consistency across the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes formatting and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Put footnotes at the bottom of the page and use 9 point font. They may be numbered or referred to by asterisks or other symbols and should be separated from the text by a line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep footnotes legible and formatted according to size rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures and tables placement and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Place figures and tables in the paper near where they are first discussed, rather than at the end, if possible. Figures and tables must be at least one column wide; wrapped text within a column is not permitted. Wide figures/tables may run across both columns and may combine subfigures or tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graphics/photos should, if possible, use vector formats (PDF, EPS). Avoid low-resolution GIF/JPEG. Ensure legibility when printed on A4 and in PDF viewers at different zoom levels. Keep file sizes manageable. Do not rely on color alone to convey distinctions (accessibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure and table captions formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a caption for every figure/table; number each sequentially: 'Figure 1: Caption of the Figure.' and 'Table 1: Caption of the Table.' Captions should be placed below figures/tables, in 10 point roman type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-line captions are centered; captions longer than one line are left-aligned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility — grayscale and readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritise the accessibility of your paper. To accommodate people who are color-blind (and those printing in black-and-white), grayscale readability is strongly encouraged. Color is not forbidden, but tables and figures should not rely solely on color to convey critical distinctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Diversity & Inclusion committee tips; ensure figures are legible in grayscale and at printed sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperlinks styling
rubrics_metrics.description: Within-document and external hyperlinks should be dark blue (hex #000099), not underlined or boxed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consistent hyperlink appearance and avoid visual clutter like boxes or underlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-English text — translation and transliteration
rubrics_metrics.description: Text in languages other than English should be accompanied by translations into English, and text in scripts other than Latin should also be accompanied by transliterations into Latin script.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples (Greek with transliteration). This ensures readers who cannot read non-Latin scripts can still understand the content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations — in-text style and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations within the text appear in parentheses (Gusfield, 1997), or if the author's name appears in the text: Gusfield (1997). Append lowercase letters to the year in case of ambiguities. Cite two-author papers using both names; cite papers with more than two authors by the first author's name and 'et al.' Collapse multiple citations into a single pair of parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from using full citations as sentence constituents. Examples and recommended phrasings are provided (avoid '(Gusfield, 1997) showed that …', prefer 'Gusfield (1997) showed that …'). Submissions should accurately reference prior and related work, including code and data. If a work appeared in multiple venues, reference the refereed archival venue when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations section required
rubrics_metrics.description: ACL currently requires all submissions to have a section titled 'Limitations', which discusses the limitations of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It may not contain any additional experiments, figures or analysis. It should be placed after the conclusion section and before references, without page breaks. It does not count towards the page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical considerations section (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: ACL encourages authors to include an optional section dedicated to discussing the broader impacts and ethical considerations of the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Likewise, it may not contain any additional experiments, figures or analysis. This section should be placed after the conclusion and before references, without page breaks, and its content does not count towards the page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgments placement and anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: The acknowledgments should go immediately before the references. Their content does not count towards the page limit. Do not number the acknowledgments section. Do not include this section in the review version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure acknowledgments are omitted from anonymous review copies to maintain double-blind review.

rubrics_metrics.name: References ordering and completeness (DOIs required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gather the full set of references under the unnumbered section heading 'References' placed before any Appendices. Arrange the references alphabetically by first author. Provide as complete a citation as possible, using a consistent format (e.g., Computational Linguistics or APA). Use full names for authors, not just initials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All references are required to contain DOIs of all cited works when possible, or links to ACL Anthology pages as a second resort. Appropriate records should be found in the ACL Anthology when available. Examples for journal, non-ACL proceedings with DOI, ACL Anthology with DOI, Anthology without DOI, and arXiv examples are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices formatting and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendices are material that can be read (lemmas, formulas, proofs, tables) that are not critical to reading/understanding the paper. Appendices must conform to the 2-column format, except for math-heavy sections where single-column improves readability. Letter the appendices in sequence and provide an informative title (e.g., 'Appendix A. Title of Appendix'). The appendices come after the references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements for font, margins, etc. are the same as the main body. Review versions of appendices must follow the same anonymity guidelines as the main paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions may include non-readable supplementary material used in the work (software/data) and described in the paper. Supplementary material may report preprocessing decisions, model parameters, and other details necessary for replication. It should be supplementary rather than central to the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary material may include explanations or details of proofs/derivations, lists of features, sample inputs/outputs, pseudo-code or source code, and data. Source code and data should be separate uploads (not part of the paper). Any accompanying software/data should include licenses and documentation of research review as appropriate. Submissions that misuse supplementary material may be rejected without review. The paper should not rely on the supplementary material; reviewers will not be asked to review it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformance enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers that do not conform to these requirements may be rejected without review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the style files and all formatting rules strictly. Contact publication chairs if you cannot meet requirements (e.g., paper size, fonts).
